questions.stem: In the lungs, oxygen moves from the alveoli into the blood by diffusion. What maintains the steep concentration gradient that allows this to continue?

options.text: Active transport pumps oxygen into the blood
Breathing brings in fresh air and blood flow constantly removes oxygen, keeping the gradient steep
The alveoli produce oxygen through photosynthesis
The blood stops moving so oxygen can diffuse more easily

questions.explanation: Continuous breathing replaces the air in the alveoli with fresh, oxygen-rich air, while the blood constantly flows past, carrying oxygen away. This maintains a steep concentration gradient so diffusion continues rapidly.
